LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 AFFIRMATIVE AND NEGATIVE SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: When do we use affirmative statements?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. construct affirmative and negative sentences in varied contexts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 AFFIRMATIVE AND NEGATIVE SENTENCES
This lesson teaches Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences for Grade 7 ENGLISH.

STUDY STEPS
1. construct affirmative and negative sentences in varied contexts
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences above.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When do we use affirmative statements?
2. When do we use negative statements?
3. Why is it important to use the right sentence when saying something?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. construct affirmative and negative sentences in varied contexts

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
